title: Auto-waiting & web-first assertions
summary: Fix a flaky test: the orders list loads after a variable delay. Replace the sleep and the one-shot count with web-first assertions.
why: Most 'flaky automation' comes from sleeping for a guessed time. Web-first assertions retry until the condition is true (or the timeout hits), so they are both fast and reliable.
pitfalls: expect(await locator.count()).toBe(3) reads once — no retry.
Raising the sleep 'fixes' it on your machine and slows every run.
teachAlong: Cause: the API delay varies per request.
Effect: a fixed sleep passes some runs and fails others.
Gate: runs your test 3 times; the 2nd run gets the 1.6 s response.

requires.reason: Check the number of orders with await expect(orders).toHaveCount(3) — it retries until the list is rendered.

wrongSolutions.label: starter (sleep + one-shot count)
